0527 H3 'Reversed Lebensohl RLEB'
0528 LIST items=8 ['Only when we can PASS and partner is expected to be UNBALANCED, i.e (1M)--X--(2M), but could be (2D multi)--X--(2M) or\n  (1m)--2m\n', 'In these auctions where partner is unbalanced and often has their own suit to show then transfer Lebensohl makes less sense\n', 'Unlike Better Minor "Gucci" Lebensohl, we can just pass if we have nothing helpful to say\n', 'The auction is already live with two bids from the opposition, we need to show shape or NT feature immediately\n', '2N puts focus on finding a NT contract, promises some sort of stop(s) and is at least invitational. This 2N is\n  "Reversed" compared to standard Lebensohl in that it does not focus on splitting up strength ranges weak/invite/GF. It\n  focuses on do we have a *stop* and game try values. This is reasonable because we can always pass with a bad hand and\n  with a very weak hand opposite a very strong partner we maybe pushed towards game anyway - we often don\'t have enough\n  space to discourage them if they are doing power takeout doubles\n', '3x new suits are weak / competitive with no way to show invitational strength, i.e ~0--9(10) hcp. You must choose\n  between a game punt or competing (which is similar to the Better Minor Gucci Lebensohl 3!c bid). The motivation is to\n  get into the auction before opener shuts us out. We might compete and reopen double with a max 9/10 hcp\n', 'Double is the usual [responsive double style](#Responsive Doubles Style) which can include flattish / no stop hands\n  including a 5 card !h invite after (1S)--X--(2S)\n', 'the name doesn\'t really help, as other variations of Lebensohl might be called "Reverse" Lebensohl (without the \'d\')']

1563 H1 'System Philosophy'
1564 LIST items=16 ['Optimize for IMPs/Rubbers, that is bidding games and slams rather than yet more ways to compete for part scores\n', 'Modern bidding is competitive, where possible have agreements to allow fast auctions and competitive bids in addition to constructive\n  bids. Sharing strength and shape information quickly in the face of competition is more important than slow start\n  super scientific relay methods (though artificial bids/relays may exist later in some auctions - after competitive threats\n  are gone).\n', "Optimizing to get into the right games/slams means fewer aggressive high variance (sometimes more fun) bids, e.g.\n  [2D Intermediate Opening](#2D Intermediate Opening) is a bit difficult to construct over (though still usefully\n  competitive), but there to make other 1 level openings more precise. A Multi 2!d allows more fun aggressive bids plus\n  a place to put one strong constructive bid but loses the intermediate opening thus making a 1!d opening very vague. By\n  not playing a multi 2!d we cannot (accurately) play 5 major + 4 minor weak twos AND 6 card major weak twos (do not\n  know how many trumps partner has when it's mixed 5 or 6). We also cannot play a fun weak only 2!d, 5 or 6 card.\n", "Fewer high variance bids includes not making crazy bids - e.g. on flat hands that have little lead directing values and\n  are likely to just give away information etc. We don't need to pressure less experienced opponents if it's also going to\n  risk partner putting us in the wrong contract. Stick to the expected ranges for bids. Some places that is a tight range and\n  others it's looser (3rd position bids, P--(1!c)--1!s overcalls etc).\n", "Accept the occasional bad result due to luck in the opponents' high variance or the weaker parts of our system\n", 'Weak 2!h/2!s are 5+ (NV) 6+ (VUL) card constructive in 1st/2nd when vulnerable. When NV we require high quality 5\n  carders, aswell as a fairly tight point range (good 6 to bad 10), to keep the constructive aspect. 3rd is\n  undisciplined of course. We state that we have a constructive aspect - we specifically do not follow a wild preempt\n  style in 1st/2nd, even though there may still be bidding theory debate about benefits of aggressive bidding,\n  especially 1st position moreso than 2nd position. Going more aggressive NV at matchpoints in 1st position or\n  favourable at IMPs may have merit!\n', 'Wide ranging openings are imprecise and make judging games/slams difficult, especially in competition. Yet we do want\n  to open almost all 11 counts (perhaps not some 4--4--4--1 hands or bad majorless vulnerable hands) to compete - those\n  balanced 11 hcp hands are very frequent. Naturally we choose to use an artificial 1!c opening to limit the\n  1D/1H/1S/2C/2D openings. So called natural systems often use a prepared club and a slew of later artificial bids\n  (e.g Gazilli) in a struggle to limit themselves.\n', 'Bidding shapely hands quickly and clearly without promising many hcp is very important, whether showing 5--5/6--5\n  hands with jump rebids, weak jump shift responses or bidding with less than the standard 6 hcp over 1 level openings.\n  Limited openings really help here.\n', "The 1!c and often 2C openings are the weak points of an artificial club system. It's hard to construct accurately over\n  an intermediate 5 card 2C opening, therefore it promises 6 cards unlike many of the older 5 card variants played in\n  Precision/Swedish club systems. The competitive/preemptive benefits of 2!c with 5 cards are arguably limited compared\n  to the downsides unless you can deny a 4 card major.\n", "A Swedish like artificial 1!c opening (two way weak NT or strong) stops opponents bidding purely destructively, but when\n  they do bid aggressively the auction can be more difficult. The 1!c opening is usually a weak NT, not strong, and having\n  separate bids (1!d for 11--13 NT and 1!c for ((13)--15) helps define those hands quickly. It's somewhat arbitrary but the\n  weak hand opening 1D arguably competes better.\n", 'An unbalanced 1!d opening is nice (natural competition in !ds), but not nice enough to require playing a wide range weak\n  NT (12--15 1!c opening) or passing various 12 hcp hands (13--15 NT). We want to bid those highly frequent 11--12 hcp\n  balanced hands.\n', "any 10--15 is slightly too wide ranging. Opening 10 hcp balanced (with 1!d) would be fun, but unlikely to play as it\n  struggles with constructive accuracy for IMPs/Rubbers. Unbalanced only 16 hcp hands open 1!c strong, as\n  they are unbalanced there's a better chance of game at 24 hcp opposite any positive 8 hcp hand. Good 10 hcp hands can\n  open 1HS or 2CD. Rule of 19 applies to 1HS openings, though you may open a weak two depending on position/vulnerability\n  with 10 hcp or just downgrade some 10 hcp hands.\n", "Precisely bidding strong hands after opponents compete following our artificial 1!c can be difficult, but by playing a\n  strong 16--18 1NT opening and 2NT right after at 19--20 hcp, all strong 16--20 hcp 1!c opening hands will be\n  unbalanced. Given that we open almost all 5--3--3--2 hands (even with 5 card majors), and some 5--4--2--2 hands\n  notrumps, ~ 55% of all 16--20 hcp hands will be classified as balanced. A strong 1!c opening becomes low frequency and\n  when it does occur it's easier to bid out the shape. Removing some strong NT hands from the 1 suited opening bids to\n  improve constructive accuracy, especially in competition is a philosophy showing up in natural systems aswell - e.g.\n  Nilsland's Scanian 2C opener including 18--21 balanced hands and 2D showing 18--19 balanced in some Italian systems.\n", 'Bidding flat hands quickly is important, much like limiting HCP ranges and bidding shapely hands clearly. 5--3--3--2\n  hands with a 5 card major, except for ~11--13 hcp 5 card major hands (1!d opening constructive sequences\n  overloaded otherwise) should show a balanced hand straight away unless judgment strongly suggests otherwise.\n  5--4--2--2 hands with a long minor, and rarely 6--3--2--2, may also want to show a balanced hand. Of course there is a\n  downside to opening hands with a natural 2N opening - there is limited bidding space to find slams, but it also shuts\n  out lead directing or other actions from the opponents.\n', 'We give up a weak NT opening which is a good NV IMPs optimization and reasonable at pairs (but risks missing 4--4\n  major fits). The even stronger 16--18 NT gets a chance to bid in 3rd more often as 1st/2nd will have fewer\n  points. The risk of opening 2N with 19 HCP is low, especially compared to the clarity it gives to strong 1!c club\n  openings and the gains from many faster auctions (1N--3N, 2N--3N etc.)\n', 'Four vs Five card majors, much like mini (NV in 3rd) v.s. weak v.s. strong notrumps, there are closely balanced pros\n  and cons. There is more five card major literature to draw from when selecting one to use with artificial 1!c\n  openings. Some of the benefits of 4 card majors are lost when all balanced hands are covered by specific bids (1NT, or\n  1!c--1NT rebid, though that leaves 1!d as nebulous). 4 card majors may, with other changes, allow a natural 1!d\n  opening and free up the 2!d opening bid as a weak two.']

1568 H2 'Discards - General Advice'
1569 LIST items=18 ['give *clear* signals with highest or lowest from equals 9 from (9)87, 2 from 43(2) etc.\n', 'new suit first discard (reverse) attitude, second discard present/remaining count (not original count)\n', 'after already lead a suit (implies attitude already known), first discard is count in that same suit\n', "discarding from partner's lead suit is present/remaining count by default as attitude should be known\n", "top of honour sequences (similar to standard lead), Q from (Q)J109x etc., showing a perfect (remaining) sequence that\n  you can afford to discard from, which helps partner not worry about that suit or just understand its strength.
